messages:
evan: quick heads up — saw a noisy Xid/ECC burst in the us-west2 GPU pool this morning, autodrain quarantined 3 nodes (gpu-0123, gpu-0148, gpu-0199). scheduling pressure spiked as pods requeued to spot nodes. wondering if our current autodrain debouncer is too sensitive.

sara: can you paste the small dmesg / nvidia log for one of the nodes? curious whether it's sustained or a short burst.

evan: pasted a condensed snippet below (from gpu-0123):
```
[ 12045.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCIe ERR): 79, Ch 00000040
[ 12045.123459] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12045.123462] kernel: ecc error count: +12 in 15s
[ 12046.223001] docker: container(ev-train-32) killed
```

cheng: thanks. this looks more like a short ECC/Xid burst cluster-wide during a long-batch job, not a progressive failure. our current policy drags a node into full drain on 3 Xid events within 1m. that threshold is pretty aggressive for high-throughput experiments. suggest: add a probabilistic debounce + short quarantine window that elevates to full drain only if bursts persist across multiple windows or correlate with hw-health metrics (fan, temp, pcie-reset count).

matt: agree. also saw capacity pressure when those 3 nodes cordoned — multiple large training pods requeued to spot-preemptible pools, pushing up cost and preemptions. if we relax immediate drain we should have a fallback to migrate heavy jobs to dedicated capacity instead of spot.

oncall-jamie: +1. runbook link: <https://internal/runbooks/gpu-failure-triage>. propose change set:
- Debounce: switch to 10m sliding window with burst aggregation (top-2 windows)
- Quarantine mode: soft-taint node (no new pods that request GPUs) for 10m instead of immediate eviction
- Escalation: if mem/correctable ecc rate stays >5/min for 30m -> hard drain + replace.

sara: can you sketch the k8s taint/taint-removal flow? i want to see how we avoid disruption to in-progress jobs that can checkpoint.

evan: sketch below — keeping it lean so the kube controller and slurm adapter can both use the same signal.
```
# pseudocode
kubectl taint node gpu-0123 gpu.quarantine=soft:NoSchedule
# controller annotates node: quarantine_started_at=<ts>
# after 10m: if spike resolved -> remove taint
# if spike persists -> kubecordon + drain (graceful, checkpoint-aware)
```

cheng: also propose a metric: `gpu.xid_burst_count` (counts windows with >N xids), and `gpu.quarantine_hits` so we can roll a canary rule and measure false positives. export both to prometheus and add an alert with multi-window suppression.

ops-bot: autodrain-controller: gpu-0123 soft-tainted at 2156001300 by policy=burst-debounce-v1, reason="xid-spike:12/15s"

matt: what's the risk of letting a flaky card stay online for 10m? could it cause kernel panics and take the whole host down?

oncall-jamie: reasonable. that's why quarantine must be soft: keep node schedulable for system daemons and allow running pods to finish or checkpoint. if node-level panics are observed in the last 24h (kernel oops, nvlink resets >3) then skip soft and hard drain immediately. add that as a rule.

sara: timeline? can we run a canary policy in us-west2 only for 24h and compare `reschedule_latency`, `preemptions`, and `replacement_rate` vs baseline?

evan: plan: implement debounce + quarantine in staging today, promote canary to us-west2 tomorrow for 24h. I'll open a PR with the config and tests. action items: @cheng add prometheus metrics and alerting; @matt add migration policy for large jobs -> dedicated pool; @oncall-jamie confirm runbook update.

cheng: assigning myself for metrics, will push exporter patch and Grafana panel.

matt: will prototype migration logic, maybe a scheduler-ext to tag >8GB jobs as "dedicated-fallback".

oncall-jamie: i'll update runbook and add the kernel-panic immediate drain exception. tagging follow-ups in the runbook. :white_check_mark:

evan: thanks all — let's keep the canary small and monitoring tight. if we see >2% increase in job preemptions or >10% rise in replacement cost, rollback to previous policy.

ops-bot: note: autodrain-controller metrics: policy=burst-debounce-v1 will roll out at 2156001600 to us-west2 canary.
